meta.title: Laboratory Incident and Accident Reporting Procedure

sections.purpose: To establish a clear, mandatory procedure for reporting, documenting, investigating, and correcting all accidents, incidents, near-misses, and unsafe conditions in pharmacy laboratories to ensure personnel safety and regulatory compliance.
sections.scope: Applicable to all pharmacy laboratory personnel, including students, teaching staff, laboratory technicians, and visitors — any person present in the laboratory at the time of an incident.
procedure: Ensure immediate safety first: if there is ongoing danger (fire, chemical spill, person injured), address the immediate hazard — activate the fire alarm, use the eyewash/safety shower, or call emergency services (108 / campus emergency) before initiating paperwork.
Provide first aid to the injured person: chemical burns — flush with water for 15 minutes; cuts — apply pressure with sterile gauze; inhalation — move to fresh air immediately.
Do not move the injured person unless they are in immediate danger.
Inform the Laboratory In-charge and Department Head immediately — verbal notification within 15 minutes of the incident.
Secure the incident scene if safe to do so — do not clean up or disturb evidence until the incident has been documented and investigated.

Complete the Laboratory Accident/Incident Report Form within 24 hours of the incident: Date, time, and exact location of incident; Names of all persons involved and witnesses; Detailed description of what happened; Substances or equipment involved; Injuries sustained; First aid or emergency response provided; Immediate corrective action taken.
Near-miss incidents (no injury but potential hazard) must also be reported on the same form — near-miss reporting is mandatory and non-punitive.
Submit the completed form to the Department Head and Safety Officer.
The Safety Officer initiates a formal Root Cause Analysis (RCA) within 48 hours for all accidents involving injury or significant property damage.
RCA findings and recommended corrective actions must be documented and presented to the department within 7 days.
Implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) — assign responsibility and target completion date for each action.
Verify completion of CAPA by the Safety Officer within the specified timeline.
Maintain all incident reports, investigation records, and CAPA documentation in the laboratory safety file for a minimum of 5 years.
Conduct a departmental safety review meeting at the end of each semester to review all incidents, trends, and CAPA status.
precautions: Incident reporting is mandatory — failure to report an incident is a disciplinary offence under institutional regulations and PCI inspection requirements.
Never alter, delete, or conceal incident information — falsification of safety records is a serious regulatory violation.
Near-miss reporting is non-punitive — the purpose is hazard correction, not blame.
All serious injuries (fractures, chemical burns covering > 5% body surface, eye injuries, loss of consciousness) require immediate notification to the institutional medical officer and Principal.
Maintain a first-aid kit in every laboratory — inspect and replenish monthly; record inspection in the safety register.
Post emergency contact numbers (hospital, fire, poison control, campus security) prominently in every laboratory.
Conduct safety drills (fire evacuation, chemical spill response) at least once per semester — record attendance and drill outcome.
